global: Translate meaning and traveller intent, not Vietnamese word order.
Keep place names, dish names and local concepts consistent with translation-glossary.json.
Do not invent facts, ingredients, prices, timings, access rules or safety claims.
Safety, allergy, transport and pricing language must be literal and unambiguous.
Prefer short natural travel copy over ornate machine-translated prose.
Keep Open Phu Quoc and JoTrip brand names unchanged.
Preserve URLs, placeholders, dates, times, measurements and phone numbers exactly.
When a local term has no clean equivalent, keep the Vietnamese name and add a short local-language explanation rather than guessing.

ui: Translate bài or bài viết as article/post in editorial UI, never as song.
Translate trải nghiệm in tourism context as experience/activity, never career.
food: Do not translate names such as Bún quậy or Bún kèn into unrelated common nouns.
Keep ingredient and allergen identity exact. Nhum is sea urchin, not shrimp, oyster or noodles.
Tắc/quất in Phu Quoc food copy means calamansi in the registered glossary context.
Còi biên mai means the edible adductor muscle, not a whistle.
Ask-staff questions must refer to the same dish and ingredient as the Vietnamese source.
stories: Keep the editorial voice warm, observational and grounded.
Avoid literal Vietnamese metaphors when they sound strange in the target language.
Do not turn local names into translated objects or unrelated place names.
knowledge: Write like a practical destination handbook, not a literal translation.
Separate documented facts from legends and interpretation.
Metaphors such as đại phẫu should become natural target-language expressions such as major transformation, not medical procedures.
Nhịp sống means the rhythm of daily life in destination prose, not biological rhythm.

en: Use international travel English with concise sentences.
Prefer Phu Quoc, Duong Dong and An Thoi spellings in running English copy.
Retain Vietnamese dish names where they are useful for ordering or search.
ko: Use natural contemporary Korean travel language and polite-neutral guide tone.
Avoid dictionary-style Sino-Korean substitutions when a familiar travel expression is clearer.
Keep the Vietnamese/Latin dish name alongside Korean explanation when useful for ordering.
ru: Use natural contemporary Russian travel-guide prose, not Vietnamese syntax mapped word for word.
Keep Vietnamese dish names where transliteration would obscure what a traveller should order.
zh-Hans: Use natural Mainland Simplified Chinese travel-guide phrasing.
Keep Vietnamese or Latin names in parentheses when this helps map search or ordering.
Do not translate proper nouns by decomposing their Vietnamese words.
zh-Hant: Use natural Traditional Chinese travel-guide phrasing.
Keep Vietnamese or Latin names in parentheses when this helps map search or ordering.
fr: Use clear contemporary travel French and retain local food names where useful.
lo: When a registered local term has no Lao target in the glossary, preserve its canonical Latin/Vietnamese form rather than guessing.
